headline: From Prison to Purpose: How Genesis Asiatic Became a Force for Change
meta_description: After 20+ years in prison, Genesis Asiatic learned to read, earned his GED, and now mentors others rebuilding their lives after release.
summary_short: Genesis Asiatic spent more than two decades behind bars unable to read. Today he's helping formerly incarcerated people transform their lives.
body:
Genesis Asiatic entered prison at 23 unable to read. More than 20 years later, he walked out transformed—and determined to help others do the same.

While incarcerated, Asiatic earned his GED and became a tutor, discovering both his own capacity for learning and his gift for teaching others. That work didn't end when he was released. Today, he channels his hard-won knowledge into mentoring people rebuilding their lives after incarceration, turning his own painful journey into a roadmap for redemption.

His story reveals what's possible when someone is given access to education and opportunity behind bars. Asiatic's transformation from a man who couldn't read to an educator shows that second chances aren't just about release dates—they're about creating pathways for formerly incarcerated people to contribute meaningfully to their communities.
quick_facts: Genesis Asiatic entered prison at age 23 unable to read
Spent more than 20 years incarcerated before release
Earned his GED while in prison
Became a tutor and now mentors formerly incarcerated people
